# Technical design — order submission

Full design: this change crosses a REST API, transactional storage, asynchronous transport and an independently deployed consumer; failure and duplicate delivery are material. Ready-now R1–R4 map exactly to FR-1–FR-4. Source fixture files are evidence of declared seams, not shipped behavior. Everything below is proposed unless explicitly marked declared.

## Approach and alternatives

Persist an order and outbox row together. Return 202 only after commit, then publish committed outbox entries asynchronously. Fulfillment atomically records event identity and its durable local effect. The transport is an injected interface; this proposal neither selects a broker nor claims exactly-once delivery.

| Option | Constraint fit | Consequence | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Transactional outbox plus duplicate-safe consumer | Fits accepted analysis | Durable publication lag and operational exhaustion state | Proposed D-1/D-2 |
| Direct publish after database commit | Invalid crash window | Accepted order can be permanently unpublished | Declined design alternative |
| Publish before commit | Violates R2 | Rollback can still fulfill an order | Declined design alternative |
| Distributed database/broker transaction | Needs transport capability not evidenced | Extra coupling; no supported interface in fixture | Not selected |

## Change by surface

| Source/surface | Change | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| src/submit.mjs | REST intake using DES-1 and DES-2 | Existing seam lines 1–4; proposed implementation |
| src/contracts.mjs (new) | Shared versioned validators | Proposed D-3 |
| src/store.mjs, src/publish.mjs (new) | Transaction/outbox and bounded publication | Accepted analysis R2/R3; mechanisms proposed D-1 |
| src/fulfill.mjs, src/receipts.mjs (new) | Durable receipt/effect transaction | Existing seam lines 1–2; proposed D-2 |
| src/payment.mjs | Interface retained as upstream dependency | Declared source lines 1–6; CON-1 |

DG-1 answers which containers own writes and where the external boundaries are. It is a **proposed C4 container model expressed in standard flowchart notation**, because the intended Markdown renderer does not support native C4. Trace DES-1–DES-3, CON-1, D-1–D-3. Sources show only interface seams; topology is proposed.

```mermaid
  Client["Actor: REST client"]

  subgraph Orders["System boundary: Order submission"]
    API["Container: Order REST API"]
    DB[("Container: Transactional order and outbox store")]
    Worker["Container: Outbox publisher"]

    Worker -->|"Read committed rows; update attempts"| DB

  end

  Worker -->|"Async order.created v1; stable eventId"| Consumer
```

The client calls the API; the API uses the unchanged upstream authorization contract and commits to the order store. A separate publisher sends order.created downstream. Fulfillment owns its receipt/effect store; no cross-system database transaction is implied.

## Contracts and data

DES-1 / D-3 proposes POST /orders v1 with customerId (nonempty string), amountMinor (positive safe integer), currency (three uppercase letters), and paymentToken (nonempty string). Reject unknown/missing/wrong-type fields with 400 before calling payment or writing. This synthetic slice models a priced order envelope, not catalog pricing or line-item inventory. A successful commit returns 202 and orderId. A commit failure returns a retryable 503 without an accepted result. Preserve the upstream authorize input/output and decline behavior from src/payment.mjs; do not leak tokens in events or persisted outbox bodies.

Event order.created v1: type, version=1, eventId (stable UUID), orderId, customerId, amountMinor, currency, authorizationId, occurredAt (UTC timestamp). Version/type mismatches fail validation; use transport negative acknowledgment for retry/dead-letter handling under the existing transport adapter. Consumer does not infer newer semantics. No adapter is chosen here.

DES-2: order and outbox share one local transaction. Orders hold orderId plus envelope and authorizationId. Outbox holds eventId (unique), payload, state (pending/published/exhausted), attempts and nextAttemptAt. A worker reserves an attempt durably before send, serializes/leases dispatch for each event, and sends only committed rows. At most five automatic attempts total, with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 seconds after respective failures. Crash after reservation may consume an attempt without delivery: boundedness is preserved and exhausted rows remain visible for recovery. A transport acknowledgment marks published; a lost acknowledgment may create duplicate delivery.

DES-3: fulfillment receives eventId, validates v1, then commits a unique receipt and local durable fulfillment effect in one transaction. Duplicates acknowledge without another effect. Rollback before commit leaves no receipt/effect and causes a retryable negative acknowledgment. External irreversible fulfillment actions are outside this bounded transaction; widening to them requires an idempotency contract and renewed analysis.

## Failure behavior and interaction order

DG-2 asks when success becomes observable and how failure/retry relates to event delivery. Proposed FR-1–FR-4 / DES-2–DES-3 / D-1–D-3, grounded in accepted analysis; wire details are proposed.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  actor Client
  participant API as Order REST API
  participant Payment as Upstream payment provider
  participant Store as Order and outbox store
  participant Worker as Outbox publisher
  participant Consumer as Downstream fulfillment
  Client->>API: POST /orders
  alt Invalid input
    API-->>Client: 400 validation error, no writes or event
  else Valid input
    API->>Payment: Existing authorize contract
    alt Authorization declined
      Payment-->>API: AuthorizationDeclined
      API-->>Client: Authorization error, no order or event
    else Authorized
      Payment-->>API: authorizationId
      API->>Store: BEGIN, write order and outbox, COMMIT
      alt Commit fails
        Store-->>API: Rollback error
        API-->>Client: Retryable failure, no accepted response or event
      else Commit succeeds
        Store-->>API: Committed orderId and eventId
        API-->>Client: 202 Accepted with orderId
        Worker->>Store: Read committed pending outbox
        Store-->>Worker: order.created with stable eventId
        loop At most five total publication attempts
          Worker-)Consumer: Async order.created
          alt Transport acknowledged
            Consumer-->>Worker: Transport acknowledgment
            Worker->>Store: Mark published
            break Stop after transport acknowledgment
              Note over Worker: No further publication attempts
            end
          else Timeout or negative acknowledgment
            Worker->>Store: Record attempt, delay 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s
          end
        end
        opt Fifth attempt fails
          Worker->>Store: Mark exhausted, retain for manual recovery
        end
        opt Fulfillment processes a delivery, including duplicates
          Consumer->>Consumer: Atomic unique eventId receipt and effect
          Note over Consumer: Existing receipt means acknowledge without another effect
        end
      end
    end
  end
```

Invalid input exits before any provider call or persistence. Authorization decline exits before local writes. Failed commit rolls back both rows and emits no event. A committed request may return before the asynchronous worker starts; 202 promises persistence, not fulfillment. The attempt loop exits on transport acknowledgment and cannot exceed five attempts. The diagram's consumer processing block represents asynchronous processing and can occur before or after publisher state update; acknowledgment ordering is transport-dependent, not a claim that fulfillment waits for published state.

Payment authorization and local commit are separate boundaries. A failed local commit after authorization can leave an upstream authorization without an order. Existing compensation/expiry policy is unknown in this fixture, and this proposal adds no cancellation operation. If owner review requires a changed payment lifecycle, return that behavior to analysis rather than hiding it in implementation.

Exhausted rows are retained for an explicit operator recovery procedure that reuses the eventId; no automatic unbounded retry. Repeated POST requests are not deduplicated by eventId: event deduplication protects redelivery of an existing order, not request idempotency. Request idempotency is outside accepted scope and must be separately analyzed if required.

## Migration, rollout and rollback

Proposed additive order/outbox and receipt structures require creation before enabling intake or consumer traffic. Run contract checks first, deploy duplicate-safe consumer before enabling publisher, then enable intake. Backward compatibility: retain payment interface; event v1 becomes a new explicit contract. Rollback disables intake and publication without deleting committed outbox/receipt rows; drain or explicitly recover pending work after fixing the deployment. Destructive retention cleanup is deferred under Q-1.

| ID | Proposed choice | Alternatives and consequences | Reversibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D-1 | Stable outbox identity; five durable attempts, then exhausted | Direct publish loses events; unlimited retry violates boundedness; durable ledger adds work | Budget/delay reversible; identity migration requires care |
| D-2 | Atomic durable receipt and local effect | Memory-only dedup fails restart; separate commits can lose effects | Additive implementation; changing identity needs migration |
| D-3 | Versioned minimal request/event shape; no paymentToken in event | Unversioned/ad hoc envelope couples deployments; exposing token widens trust | New versions can coexist; shipped fields cannot silently change |

All decisions remain proposed. Dependent tasks explicitly name them in requires_decisions. There is no acceptance actor/date or start receipt.
